sources.title: About – Newton Lab
sources.text: Skip to content Newton Lab University of California San Diego About Play Our Research Our lab investigates the basic molecular mechanisms of how cells transduce information, a process know as cell signaling. We focus on a key signaling enzyme, protein kinase C , which is generally a little too active in neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s Disease, and not active enough in many cancers. Understanding protein kinase C mechanisms is a first step in developing therapies to restore (cancer) or inhibit (Alzheimer’s Disease) protein kinase C so that it functions normally. We also study the phosphatase PHLPP which has many cellular functions, including opposing protein kinase C signaling. PUBLICATIONS

Alexandra C. Newton, Ph.D. Distinguished Professor of Pharmacology Director, Cell Signaling San Diego
sources.text: Alexandra C. Newton, Ph.D. Distinguished Professor of Pharmacology Director, Cell Signaling San Diego FACULTY PROFILE STYLESHEET: do not remove this block Alexandra C. Newton, Ph.D. Distinguished Professor of Pharmacology Director, Cell Signaling San Diego Research Interests Our lab focusses on the molecular mechanisms by which disruption of the balance between phosphorylation and dephosphorylation drives disease. We focus in particular on understanding how deregulated signaling by protein kinases and phosphatases is involved in cancer vs degenerative diseases. We are particularly interested in protein kinase C and related kinases such as Akt, and the protein phosphate PH domain Leucine rich repeat Protein Phosphatase PHLPP (pronounced ‘flip’).
